extracted.intended_audience: students, critics, and practitioners of poetry and drama (poets, playwrights, literary scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for composing and judging dramatic and romantic poetry (esp. stage drama), including appropriate subject-matter, modes of representation, structural requirements, and kinds of dramatic conclusion. Draws on examples from Spanish theatre (Cervantes, Lope de Vega, Calderón), the ancients, and moderns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over‑nicety (Ahudeza)
rubrics_metrics.description: The danger of degenerating from extreme accuracy and acuteness into a sort of over nicety — Ahudeza; Spanish prose often struggled with this, though Cervantes shows no trace of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let precision harden into finickiness; aim for clarity and naturalness rather than hyper‑fastidious stylistic effect. Use Cervantes as a model where accuracy does not become affectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Richness of spirit and invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Works of wit should be 'richest in spirit and invention' and give a lively and altogether epic picture of life and national character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond technical perfection of style, value imaginative richness and the capacity to paint a vivid national or social picture; this is part of what makes a work enduring (example: Don Quixote).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adorn narrative with poetic effusion to preserve poetical title
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer should be careful so to adorn with a rich effusion of poetry his narrative, machinery, and the whole of his language, as to preserve undegraded his title to the name of a poet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When prose or narrative aspires to be poetic, integrate poetry into narrative and diction (mirth, seriousness, wit, and poetry should be mingled) so the work sustains its claim to poetry rather than collapsing into mere satire or prose wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect representation of the present is generally preferable
rubrics_metrics.description: The indirect representation of the actual and the present is the best and most appropriate; the true poet lends poetic illumination to commonplace things rather than depicting the present with uncompromising precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To make present life poetic, veiling or mediating devices (history, national traditions, myth, the past) allow extraction of deeper meaning; direct literal realism risks binding the fancy and producing over‑precise description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry represents the eternal through a veil; needs corporeal habitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper business of poetry is to represent only the eternal ... but this cannot be accomplished without the intervention of a veil. Poetry requires to have a corporeal habitation, and this she finds in her best sphere, the traditions of a nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to express universal/eternal meanings but ground them in national tradition, stories, or concrete material so the 'veil' mediates abstract truth into embodied representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet may succeed despite choosing an inadequate subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The true poet can shew his power even though he takes a wrong way, and composes works which are far from perfection in regard to their original foundation (e.g., Milton and Klopstock).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not dismiss works solely for imperfect subject choice—assess craft and poetic power as well as subject appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic poetry implies a nation and needs a metropolis
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic poetry is the production of the city and society; it cannot flourish unless it have a great metropolis to be the centre point of its development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the importance of social/institutional infrastructure (theatre culture, audiences, metropolitan centers) in developing sustained dramatic art (examples: Madrid, London, Paris).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of arrangement and steady law required for the stage
rubrics_metrics.description: A strength of arrangement, and a steady law, are so much the more necessary for the stage, because in no other species of composition are carelessness and corruption so easily tolerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plays demand rigorous structure and disciplined plotting; theatrical success should not be allowed to substitute for sound arrangement and coherent dramatic law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatre requires clear plan and profound purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a play's plan be clearly laid, and its purpose profoundly considered, they want the very essence of dramatic pieces; they may amuse but lack deep sense and import.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that dramatic works have an underlying conceptual purpose and a clear plan, not just surface passions or spectacles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three orders/ends of dramatic art (surface → knowledge → resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: First order: plays presenting the visible surface of life alone; Second order: dramatists who display a deeper knowledge of man and life; Third (higher) end: the art should not merely express the enigma of life but solve it, entwining the future with the present and revealing internal mysteries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or composing drama, identify which order the work aspires to. Higher drama should aim beyond depiction toward insight and resolution of human dilemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three modes of dramatic conclusion (destruction, reconciliation, glorification/purification)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three terminations: (1) total ruin/destruction of the hero (e.g., Wallenstein, Macbeth, Faustus), (2) reconciliation/partial consolation (some ancient tragedies end with soothing melancholy), (3) spiritual purification or glorification where out of misery and death a new life arises (favored by Christian poets like Calderón).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an appropriate mode of denouement for thematic aims; ensure the ending arises organically from the drama (and in the best cases carries internal meaning, not merely external catastrophe).

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher/spiritual subjects need indirect embodiment in terrestrial materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The invisible world, the Deity, and pure intellects, can never, upon the whole, be with propriety represented by us; the higher and spiritual world can be everywhere embodied and shadowed forth in our terrestrial materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When treating spiritual or abstract matters, personify or embody them within concrete scenes, characters, and events rather than attempting literal depiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romanticism as Christian‑inflected feeling (sorrows as way to happiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The romantic consists entirely in that feeling of love which is predominant in the Christian religion, by which sorrows are represented as only the way to happiness ... the romantic is by no means inconsistent with the ancients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Romantic elements (love, purification through suffering, hopeful play of fancy) are compatible with epic/ancient models; use romantic feeling to soften tragic seriousness and to select forms harmonious with that feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid theatrical routine and demagogic corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Theatrical success is the strongest and most irresistible in its operation on the vanity of a poet; the public themselves are in general the first to spoil a favourite dramatist, producing negligence in composition (example: Lope de Vega).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist letting audience approval or routine stage formulas supplant artistic care. Maintain standards even under popular demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid/careless composition tolerable in popular poetry but not in the theatre
rubrics_metrics.description: Although our indulgence may be due to a rapid and careless method of composition in popular poetry, the theatre has no similar claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not excuse slovenly or improvised playwriting; theatrical works require more deliberation and craft than ephemeral popular verse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using episodic devices merely to create poetic distance for the author
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors frequently introduce travelling adventures, duels, elopements, bandits, or strollers, often more for the sake of the author than of his hero, to procure poetic distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If employing exotic episodes or devices to escape realism, ensure they serve character and plot authentically rather than functioning as authorial shortcuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic art should display deep knowledge of human nature and life
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic representations should display a deep knowledge, not of individuals and their affairs alone, but of our whole species, of the world and of life, in all their manifold shapes, contradictions, and catastrophes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess plays on their capacity to illuminate universal aspects of human existence and to handle contradictions and complexities of life with insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragic destruction should arise from hero's free will and guilt, not arbitrary fate
rubrics_metrics.description: A tragedy of destruction is more perfect insofar as the destruction is represented not as anything external, capricious, or predestinated, but as a darkness into which the hero has sunk step by step, in consequence of his own guilt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose or judge tragic arcs so that downfall follows believable moral/character causes—avoid deus ex machina or arbitrary fate as sole causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Christian dramatist's Christianity lies in feeling and method, not mere external circumstance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Christianity of Calderón does not consist so much in the external circumstances which he has selected, as in his peculiar feeling, and the method of treating his subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When integrating religious/spiritual themes, focus on tone, moral sensibility, and method of treatment to achieve genuine spiritual effect rather than relying on overtly religious plot elements alone.
